answer: DNS Spoofing, also known as DNS cache poisoning, involves adversaries manipulating DNS settings to redirect users from legitimate websites to malicious ones. This can be achieved by injecting false DNS responses into the cache of a DNS resolver, causing users to be directed to incorrect IP addresses. The attackers may use this technique to prevent access to legitimate sites or to deliver malware [Source 1].
